summary: StratosCargo private deployment: TLS renegotiation storm caused partial transcript loss; urgent customer escalation
description: Issue summary: Between 2024-11-02 15:05 and 2024-11-02 15:40 UTC StratosCargo began seeing intermittent streaming truncation and missing transcript segments from their private VPC deployment. Impact: ~18% of streaming completions returned truncated transcripts (client received EOT prematurely) and ~6% of requests resulted in silent streaming resets. Customer reports production user-facing failures and requested immediate remediation and SLA credit. Environment: Private deployment (vpc-connect) hosted in us-central, running private control plane v2.3.1 and inference nodes on GPU pool 'private-usc-phi'. Immediate ask: identify root cause, mitigate to restore streaming reliability to >99.9%, and agree next steps for rollback/patch and customer SLA remedy.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer long-running chat session with streaming enabled and model redwood-llm-13b-quantized-v1 pinned.
2) Send multi-turn prompts with frequent resets of client-side TLS session (simulated NAT timeouts).
3) Observe intermittent early stream termination and missing transcript ranges.
4) Reproduce more reliably by triggering TLS renegotiation at burst rates (NAT rebind + client reconnects).

investigation_notes: Hypotheses: 1) Client-side aggressive TLS renegotiation + private NAT behaviour causing session churn and premature stream resets. 2) TLS renegotiation path triggers a short-lived state where serving-runtime drops active stream checkpoint leading to transcript gaps. 3) Rate limiter/autoscaler reaction created a brief resource pressure window on node-07, exacerbating resets. Findings: - Reproduced spike by simulating TLS session churn; early-eof correlates with active TLS renegotiation window (~200-400ms). - Kernel selection / quantized model execution continues but session affinity mapping to streaming multiplexer briefly returned 502-like resets. - Node-level metrics show CPU and epoll wake spikes coincident with handshake bursts. - No evidence of data corruption on disk or model weights. Related artifacts: dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/streaming/stratos-tls-storm, packet captures uploaded to S3: s3://redwood-support/stratos/tls-storm-pcaps/
comments: Maya Patel (Support) 2024-11-02T15:18Z: Acknowledged with customer and opened incident. Notified SRE and Private Deploy team. Customer reports user-visible truncation, requested ETA for mitigation.

Diego Alvarez (SRE) 2024-11-02T15:25Z: Initial triage: saw TLS renegotiation bursts on node-07. Spinning up node-09 as hot spare and enabling conservative reconnect backoff for customer route. Requesting traffic mirroring to test cluster.

Aisha Khan (Private Deploy Eng) 2024-11-02T15:40Z: Found that our TLS stack allowed renegotiation to skip stream resume handshake in the multiplexer when handshake overlapped with chunk flush. Applying short-term patch to hold stream state until handshake completion. Will deploy to canary group now.

StratosCargo (Customer) 2024-11-02T16:00Z: Thank you for quick response—we saw improvement after you enabled backoff. Please confirm what caused this and what the compensation will be for impacted customers.

Diego Alvarez (SRE) 2024-11-03T09:12Z: Canary patch confirmed in canary (node-09/10), dropped truncated streams below 0.3%. Scheduling full rollout 2024-11-03T10:00Z with monitoring and rollback on failure. Preparing customer-facing incident summary and SLA credit calculation.
Maya Patel (Support) 2024-11-04T11:48Z: Incident resolved with full rollout complete. Preparing formal post-incident follow-up and credit offer.
resolution: Mitigation steps: 1) Applied a hotfix to the private TLS multiplexer to defer stream state teardown until TLS renegotiation completes and stream chunks are flushed. 2) Enabled conservative reconnect/backoff policy for StratosCargo route to reduce NAT-triggered handshake storms. 3) Added temporary node headroom (scaled private-usc-phi pool + spun up node-09) during remediation window. Rollout notes: patch rolled to canary at 2024-11-02T15:50Z, observed drop in truncated streams from 18%->0.3% in canary, full rollout completed 2024-11-03T10:20Z. Post-incident customer action: Support offered SLA credit and scheduled 2024-11-06 deep-dive call. Root cause: overlap between client-initiated TLS renegotiation and the streaming multiplexer teardown path exposed a race that caused early EOFs and missing transcript fragments under high renegotiation rates. Engineering fix: patch to multiplexer to await handshake completion and explicit chunk-flush acknowledgement before session teardown. Monitoring and prevention: added alerting for TLS renegotiation rate >10/s per node, introduced canary traffic test that simulates NAT rebind scenarios, and updated the private-deploy runbook.
postincident_action_items: Deploy multiplexer race-condition unit tests into CI to cover TLS renegotiation overlap
Add synthetic canary that simulates NAT rebind/TLS renegotiation to PR gate and canary pipelines
Update private-deploy runbook with explicit TLS renegotiation troubleshooting steps
Create customer communication template for private TLS incidents and SLA credit process
Schedule cross-team retro (SRE, Private Deploy, Networking) for 2024-11-08
